relations.support_notes: This is confirmed by the contents of the work, despite the ambiguous phrasing in the introductory verses suggesting it is a commentary on the Sūtrasamuccaya (mdo sde kun las btus pa'i don || gsal byed nyi ma'i snying po 'di ||), as does the name of the work given in the colophon (mdo sde kun las buts pa'i Ti ka mdo'i nyi ma'i snying po).

relations.zotero_refs: Author according to [8H6M69W4], No. 15506: nyang gi slob ma. This reflects the colophon's remark that the author relied on "chos kyi ye shes" (taking "chos kyi ye shes" to refer to Nyang bran chos kyi ye shes).

comments:
The work description in the closing verses (mdo sde kun las btus pa'i don...) and colophon (mdo sde kun las btus pa'i ti ka) indicates a commentary on the Sūtrasamuccaya (ID:3738), but in terms of its contents, the work is a commentary on the Śikṣāsamuccaya (ID:3742). 

According to the colophon ex21022023-09-181, gZhon nu rin chen relies on the explanations of "Chos kyi ye shes" - this is Nyang bran Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) in view of the reference to "Nyang gi bran" in the conclusive verses - and that of "brTson 'grus seng ge," likely gTsang nag pa (ID:3839), as the latter was a student of Nyang bran.
The author refers with name to Atiśa ("jo bo chen po", (ID:3745)), Lo tsha ba=rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786), and Nyang bran (ID:3876), and refers anonymously to the views of other Tibetan scholars, some of whom (Zhang tshes (ID:3805), Lo tsha ba (ID:3786), sTag lo (ID:7033), Khyung (ID:3809), etc.) are identified in interlinear glosses in instance (ID:4624); the glosses are concentrated in the first 12 folios then resume at two-thirds of the text on after a long break.

The work could correspond to the "bslab btus Tik+ka" listed by A khu ching shes rab rgya mtsho in his Tho yig ([5RXEUKD9]: 514, No. 11073: gzhon nu rin chen gyi bslab btus Tik+ka).
